sq.q: 1)Define address binding. What are the types of address binding?
answer: Address binding is the process of mapping logical addresses (used by programs) to physical addresses (used by hardware). There are three types of address binding:
Compile-time binding – if memory location is known at compile time.
Compile-time binding – if memory location is known at compile time.
Load-time binding – if address is determined at program load.
Load-time binding – if address is determined at program load.
Execution-time binding – if address changes during execution (used in dynamic memory allocation).
Execution-time binding – if address changes during execution (used in dynamic memory allocation).

lq.q: What is Address Binding? Explain its Types with a Diagram
answer: Address binding is the process of mapping logical addresses (also known as virtual addresses) to physical addresses (actual memory locations in RAM).

When a program is executed, the CPU generates addresses during instruction execution. These addresses must be translated to actual locations in main memory — and this is done through address binding .
There are three main types of address binding, based on when the binding takes place:
Occurs when the program is compiled .
